title: Product Vision Alignment
questionDetail: How does your product team ensure that the technical vision aligns with business objectives? Discuss specific frameworks, communication patterns, and feedback loops you use to maintain this alignment throughout the product lifecycle.
answerDetails: Successful alignment requires multiple touchpoints: regular syncs for immediate concerns, OKRs for measurable goals, and technical roadmaps for long-term vision. The key is creating bidirectional communication channels.

title: Developer Experience Impact
questionDetail: When making product decisions, how do you measure and prioritize the impact on developer experience? Share examples of trade-offs you've made between feature velocity and developer satisfaction.
answerDetails: A balanced scorecard approach considers both immediate business needs and long-term developer productivity. This includes metrics like deployment frequency, MTTR, developer NPS, and feature delivery rates.

title: Technical Debt Prioritization
questionDetail: How does your product team work with engineering to prioritize technical debt alongside new features? Describe your framework for making these decisions and communicating them to stakeholders.
answerDetails: Risk-based prioritization evaluates technical debt by its impact on security, performance, developer velocity, and customer experience. This creates a common language between product and engineering.

title: API Design Philosophy
questionDetail: What role does the product team play in API design decisions? Discuss how you balance developer ergonomics with business requirements when defining API contracts.
answerDetails: Collaborative API design ensures both business needs and developer experience are considered. Product brings use cases and user journeys while engineering provides technical constraints and best practices.

title: Developer Tool Investment
questionDetail: How do you build the business case for investing in internal developer tools and platforms? Share your approach to quantifying ROI on developer productivity improvements.
answerDetails: Comprehensive analysis includes time savings, reduced incidents, faster onboarding, improved retention, and increased feature velocity. Combine quantitative metrics with qualitative feedback.

title: Documentation Standards
questionDetail: What standards does your product team set for technical documentation? Discuss how you ensure documentation remains accurate and valuable throughout the product lifecycle.
answerDetails: Shared responsibility ensures documentation stays current. Product defines user journeys and use cases, engineering provides technical details, and both review for accuracy and completeness.

title: Feature Flag Strategy
questionDetail: How does your product team leverage feature flags for progressive rollouts? Describe your decision framework for flag usage and the collaboration model with engineering.
answerDetails: Joint frameworks define flag types (release, experiment, ops, permission), ownership models, lifecycle management, and success criteria. This enables safe, controlled feature delivery.

title: Developer Onboarding
questionDetail: What role does product play in optimizing the developer onboarding experience? Discuss how you measure success and iterate on the onboarding process.
answerDetails: Cross-functional ownership ensures comprehensive onboarding. Product defines success metrics (time to first commit, time to productivity), while teams collaborate on content and delivery.

title: Platform vs Feature Balance
questionDetail: How do you balance platform improvements against feature development? Share your framework for allocating resources between foundational work and customer-facing features.
answerDetails: Dynamic allocation responds to current needs while maintaining minimum platform investment. Consider technical debt, scalability needs, developer velocity, and business goals quarterly.

title: Developer Feedback Loops
questionDetail: What mechanisms does your product team use to gather and act on developer feedback? Describe how this feedback influences your roadmap and priority decisions.
answerDetails: Continuous channels include regular surveys, office hours, Slack channels, retros, and embedded product managers. Quick response to feedback builds trust and improves outcomes.

title: Security in Product Design
questionDetail: How early does your product team engage with security considerations? Discuss your approach to building security into the product development lifecycle rather than treating it as an afterthought.
answerDetails: Continuous involvement includes threat modeling during design, security champions in product teams, regular security reviews, and security acceptance criteria in stories.

title: Performance Requirements
questionDetail: How does your product team define and communicate performance requirements? Share examples of how you've balanced feature richness with performance constraints.
answerDetails: Collaborative SLO setting involves product defining user experience goals (page load time, response time) while engineering provides technical feasibility and measurement strategies.

title: Developer Advocacy Metrics
questionDetail: What metrics does your product team track to measure the success of developer advocacy initiatives? Discuss how these metrics influence product decisions.
answerDetails: Comprehensive metrics include developer NPS, adoption rates, time to value, support ticket volume, community engagement, and contribution rates. These guide product investments.

title: Technical Feasibility Assessment
questionDetail: How does your product team assess technical feasibility before committing to features? Describe your process for early technical validation and risk assessment.
answerDetails: Continuous assessment includes technical spikes, proof of concepts, architecture reviews, and early engineering involvement. This reduces late-stage surprises and pivots.

title: API Versioning Strategy
questionDetail: How does your product team approach API versioning and deprecation? Discuss the balance between innovation and backward compatibility in your decision-making.
answerDetails: Usage-based deprecation considers active users, migration complexity, and business impact. Clear communication timelines and migration tools support smooth transitions.

title: Developer Community Building
questionDetail: What role does product play in building and nurturing the developer community? Share strategies for creating engaged, contributing developer ecosystems.
answerDetails: Distributed ownership leverages product for strategy and roadmap engagement, engineering for technical leadership, and marketing for reach. Coordination is key.

title: Internal Tool Prioritization
questionDetail: How do you prioritize internal developer tools against external features? Discuss your framework for making these investment decisions.
answerDetails: ROI-based decisions quantify developer productivity gains, reduced time to market, and quality improvements against direct revenue features. Both are essential.

title: Developer Success Metrics
questionDetail: How does your product team define and measure developer success? Share specific KPIs and how they connect to business outcomes.
answerDetails: Holistic metrics include deployment frequency, lead time, MTTR, change failure rate (DORA metrics), plus developer satisfaction, retention, and growth. These predict business success.

title: Technical Partnership Model
questionDetail: How does your product team partner with platform and infrastructure teams? Describe the collaboration model and decision rights.
answerDetails: Integrated planning aligns platform capabilities with product needs. Regular syncs, shared OKRs, and joint architecture reviews ensure cohesive evolution.

title: Innovation Time Allocation
questionDetail: How does your product team support engineering innovation time? Discuss how you balance directed work with exploration and experimentation.
answerDetails: Integrated innovation weaves experimentation into regular work through spike stories, POCs, and innovation sprints. This balances exploration with delivery.
